items.title: Alibaba vs. Uber Technologies: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: This article compares Alibaba Group and Uber Technologies, assessing which stock is a better buy for investors in 2026. It delves into the business models, financial performance, risk profiles, and valuation metrics of both companies. The author ultimately recommends Uber due to its diversified platform, accelerating growth, and substantial free cash flow, contrasting it with Alibaba's geopolitical risks despite its strong fundamentals.

items.title: Infrastructure: Today’s “Generational” Investment Opportunity
items.summary: Apollo Global Management's partners Harry Seekings and Vittorio Lacagnina discuss infrastructure as a "generational" investment opportunity, driven by immense capital expenditure needs in areas like AI, digitization, and power grid modernization. They highlight infrastructure's appeal due to stable cash flows, inflation protection, low correlation to public markets, and its ability to solve portfolio problems for investors. The article emphasizes that infrastructure provides essential services across economic cycles and is becoming more accessible to a wider range of investors.

items.title: Marathon Petroleum stock hits all-time high at 431.23 USD By Investing.com
items.summary: Marathon Petroleum (MPC) stock has reached an all-time high of $431.23, marking a 163% year-to-date return. This surge is attributed to positive investor sentiment, strong financial health, and rising oil prices amidst Middle Eastern tensions. While UBS maintains a "Buy" rating with a $450 price target, Jefferies downgraded the stock to "Hold" due to refining risk-reward dynamics.

items.title: Chipotle Sinks 4% as Selling Outruns the Restaurant Group; McDonald’s and Starbucks Dip
items.summary: Chipotle stock has fallen 4% and is extending a month-long slide, dropping 19% over the past month and nearing its 52-week low. This decline is significantly sharper than that of its rivals, McDonald's and Starbucks, which saw drops of less than 1%. The selling is attributed to margin pressure from beef and freight inflation, despite revenue growth, and an options market signaling further potential downside.

items.title: ConocoPhillips forecasts oil will be near US$70 per barrel
items.summary: ConocoPhillips President Ryan Lance predicts that oil prices will find a floor near US$70 per barrel, with mid-cycle West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude possibly ranging between US$65 and US$70. Lance anticipates U.S. oil production could surpass 14 million barrels per day, supported by current prices, while global oil demand may fully recover by 2028-2029, continuing to grow thereafter. The company is prioritizing upstream investments to meet this anticipated future demand.

items.title: Ross Stores (ROST) Q1 2025 Earnings: Results, Market Reaction & History | 24/7 Wall St.
items.summary: Ross Stores (ROST) reported Q1 2025 earnings, slightly beating EPS and revenue estimates, with GAAP diluted EPS at $1.47 and revenue at $4.98 billion. Despite a slow start to the quarter, sales momentum picked up, though comparable store sales remained flat. The company withdrew its full-year guidance due to tariff-related uncertainty and projected Q2 EPS between $1.40 and $1.55, accounting for a significant tariff cost headwind.

items.title: ConocoPhillips chair Ryan Lance on oil price floor outlook
items.summary: ConocoPhillips Executive Chairman Ryan Lance anticipates the oil price floor to rise to $70 per barrel, with U.S. West Texas Intermediate stabilizing between $65 and $70. He also projected that U.S. oil output could exceed 14.5 million barrels per day if prices remain consistent. Lance cautioned that global oil demand might stay depressed until late 2020s, with significant rebound expected around 2028-2029, and highlighted ConocoPhillips' focus on upstream investments.

items.title: Morgan Stanley cuts AutoNation, Group 1 as dealer headwinds mount
items.summary: Morgan Stanley has downgraded AutoNation and Group 1 Automotive, citing negative earnings revisions, rising interest rates and oil prices, and regulatory/technological challenges for franchise auto dealers. The firm expects Street estimates to decrease further as Q3 results are released, noting pressure is extending beyond vehicle-margin normalization into higher-margin ancillary businesses. Despite structural risks, Morgan Stanley reiterated Carvana as its top pick due to its vertically integrated, digital model.

items.title: Mid Penn Backs $2.38 Million Philadelphia Housing Project
items.summary: Mid Penn Bank is providing $1.9 million in construction financing for a $2.38 million affordable-homeownership project in Philadelphia's Brewerytown neighborhood. This initiative, part of the city's Turn the Key program, will develop 10 new homes. The project aims to offer income-qualified, first-time buyers new homes at an anticipated sale price of $280,000, with construction expected to finish in spring 2027.

items.title: Citigroup Reports Q3 Earnings on October 13 After a Yield-Driven Bank Selloff. Here’s What the Stock Needs to Show
items.summary: Citigroup is set to report its Q3 earnings on October 13, following a recent bank selloff driven by rising Treasury yields. The article highlights key metrics investors should focus on, such as net credit losses, delinquencies, and loan growth, rather than just EPS, given the market's concerns about credit quality. It also notes that a potential $9 billion Banamex charge is anticipated in 2027, which could impact reported earnings that year.
